A 30% markup is not a 30% margin.

If a commercial cleaning job costs $2,000/month:
• 30% markup = $2,600
• 30% margin = about $2,857

That gap can quietly erase profit on recurring contracts.

Free labor-first bid calculator: https://offerpeek.com/tools/commercial-cleaning-bid-calculator/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=cleaning_bid

Commercial cleaning bids get easier when you stop guessing from a price-per-square-foot number.

A cleaner sequence is:
1. Scope the job
2. Estimate labor hours
3. Add loaded labor + supplies
4. Add overhead
5. Apply target margin

Free calculator: https://offerpeek.com/tools/commercial-cleaning-bid-calculator/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=cleaning_bid

A janitorial proposal should make three things obvious to the buyer: what is included, how often it is done, and what it costs.

The fastest way to lose margin on an office-cleaning contract is to under-estimate labor.

Before quoting, separate cleanable square footage, production rate, visit frequency and loaded wage cost. The selling price should come last—not first.

Most prospect lists answer one question: “Who exists?”

That is not the same as knowing who may actually need what you sell.

AI Opportunity Research looks for visible evidence of a business problem, then ranks the opportunity by AI need, buying potential and solution fit.

50 or 100 evidence-verified opportunities:
https://karadagsatis.gumroad.com/l/ai-opportunity-research-pack?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ai_opportunity_research

5,000 scraped records can still leave you with hours of filtering.

A smaller list can be more useful when every business includes:
• visible evidence of need
• source URLs
• AI Need score
• Buyability score
• recommended solution
• a personalized outreach angle

That is the idea behind the AI Opportunity Research Pack:
https://karadagsatis.gumroad.com/l/ai-opportunity-research-pack?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ai_opportunity_research

Before contacting a business about AI automation, I want to know one thing:

Why this company?

Not just its industry. Not just its size.

What visible operational gap suggests that an AI receptionist, chatbot, workflow automation or another AI solution could actually help?

That “why” is what this research pack is built around.
https://karadagsatis.gumroad.com/l/ai-opportunity-research-pack?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ai_opportunity_research

Prospecting stack:
Database → filters → enrichment → manual research → qualification → outreach.

For a small AI agency, that can become a job by itself.

An alternative is to start with fewer businesses that have already been researched for need, buying potential and solution fit.

AI Opportunity Research Pack:
https://karadagsatis.gumroad.com/l/ai-opportunity-research-pack?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ai_opportunity_research

A prospect should not make the list just because it matches an industry filter.

A stronger opportunity has evidence.

Examples:
• manual booking or intake
• repeated service-response complaints
• obvious workflow friction
• missing automation where the business volume appears to justify it

Research the problem first. Sell the solution second.
